mappings.note: This verse describes the preparation of the fish and the three days/nights. This content is entirely absent from the provided OSMAIN text (which starts with Jona praying inside the fish). The OSMAIN text appears to be missing the introductory narrative found in standard Bible texts.
Translation v2 ('Or, Jonas fit sa prière...') corresponds exactly to OSMAIN v1 ('Da ba Jona til Herren sin Gud fra fiskens indre.').
Translation v3 matches OSMAIN v2 ('I min nød ropte jeg til Herren...').
Translation v4 matches OSMAIN v3 ('Du kastet meg ned i dypet...').
Translation v5 matches OSMAIN v4 ('Jeg tenkte: Jeg er drevet bort...').
Translation v6 matches OSMAIN v5 ('Vannet omsluttet meg helt til strupen...').
Translation v7 matches OSMAIN v6 ('Jeg sank ned til fjellenes røtter...').
Translation v8 matches OSMAIN v7 ('Da min sjel vansmektet i meg...').

The translation contains a significant theological expansion not found in the OSMAIN text. OSMAIN v8 says: 'De som holder seg til tomme avguder, vender ryggen til nåden som kunne vært deres.' (Those who cling to empty idols turn their backs on the grace that could have been theirs). The translation says: 'Ceux qui s'attachent à des vanités trompeuses abandonnent celui qui leur fait miséricorde;' (Those who attach themselves to deceptive vanities abandon the one who shows them mercy). The concept of 'abandoning the one who shows mercy' is an addition/interpretation not present in the Norwegian text.
Translation v10 matches OSMAIN v9 ('Men jeg vil ofre til deg med lovsang...').
Translation v11 matches OSMAIN v10 ('Da befalte Herren fisken...').

extraContent.description: Entire verse missing from OSMAIN: 'Et l'Éternel prépara un grand poisson pour engloutir Jonas, et Jonas fut dans le ventre du poisson trois jours et trois nuits.' (The Lord prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights).

Phrase added/expanded: 'abandonnent celui qui leur fait miséricorde' (abandon the one who shows them mercy). The OSMAIN text only says they turn their backs on 'grace that could have been theirs', not that they abandon God directly.
